header.subtitle: Module 12: The Developer of the Future
sec.mudanca.h2: The developer of the future does not compete with agents. They architect the system where agents work.
sec.mudanca.intro: P11 showed that agents can remember, retrieve, execute, and learn. The question now is more important: what is the human role when implementation is no longer the main bottleneck?
sec.mudanca.dev2018.label: Developer 2018
sec.mudanca.dev2018.title: Efficient implementer
sec.mudanca.dev2018.desc: Value was measured by turning tickets into code, knowing syntax, and navigating the framework quickly.
sec.mudanca.dev2023.label: Developer 2023
sec.mudanca.dev2023.title: Augmented copilot user
sec.mudanca.dev2023.desc: Value was measured by using autocomplete, chat, and snippets to speed up human-centered implementation.
sec.mudanca.dev2026.label: Developer 2026
sec.mudanca.dev2026.title: Architect of agents
sec.mudanca.dev2026.desc: Value is measured by defining intent, context, boundaries, verification, and responsibility for the result.
sec.mudanca.thesis.label: Session thesis
sec.mudanca.thesis.body: The problem is not writing code faster. It is deciding which code should exist, how it should fit into the system, and what evidence proves it is correct.
sec.agentic.intro: An agentic flow is not sending a big prompt and hoping. It is a cycle where the human defines intent, the agent proposes and executes, and the verification system decides what can move forward.
sec.agentic.step1.title: Intent
sec.agentic.step1.desc: Goal, user, constraints, non-goals, and acceptance criteria.
sec.agentic.step2.title: Plan
sec.agentic.step2.desc: The agent proposes decomposition, files, risks, and validation strategy.
sec.agentic.step3.title: Calibration
sec.agentic.step3.desc: The human adjusts architecture, scope, trade-offs, and sensitive areas.
sec.agentic.step4.title: Execution
sec.agentic.step4.desc: The agent edits code, queries tools, runs commands, and records decisions.
sec.agentic.step5.title: Verification
sec.agentic.step5.desc: Tests, hooks, reviewers, logs, and observability filter what is safe.
sec.agentic.step6.title: Learning
sec.agentic.step6.desc: Useful lessons become memory, rules, tests, or workflow adjustments.
sec.agentic.prompt.title: The difference between asking for code and directing work
sec.agentic.bad.label: Loose prompt
sec.agentic.bad.desc: The AI has to guess scope, permissions, format, performance, errors, audit, and tests.
sec.agentic.good.label: Controlled delegation
sec.agentic.good.desc: The human does not choose every line, but defines the right solution space.
sec.arquetipos.h2: The four archetypes of new seniority
sec.arquetipos.intro: They may become separate roles in large companies, but in smaller teams the same developer shifts between these roles throughout a task. Seniority becomes a composition, not a single title.
sec.arquetipos.system.title: Systems Architect
sec.arquetipos.system.desc: Designs the shape of the system, defines contracts, scale, infrastructure, constraints, and where agents can operate without breaking the architecture.
sec.arquetipos.orchestrator.title: AI Orchestrator / Context Engineer
sec.arquetipos.orchestrator.desc: Creates context pipelines, decomposes work, chooses tools, prepares docs, rules, examples, tests, and feedback loops.
sec.arquetipos.product.title: Product Engineer
sec.arquetipos.product.desc: Translates real needs into testable behavior, validates whether software solves the use case, and cuts scope that does not serve the product.
sec.arquetipos.quality.title: Quality & Reliability Lead
sec.arquetipos.quality.desc: Reviews AI outputs, hunts edge cases, designs tests, watches technical debt, and ensures speed does not become regression at scale.
sec.competencias.intro: Syntax and boilerplate are still useful, but they stop being differentiators. The weight shifts to intent, context, system design, verification, and judgment.
sec.competencias.intent.title: Intent Architecture
sec.competencias.intent.desc: Goal, acceptance criteria, limits, and non-goals.
sec.competencias.context.title: Context Engineering
sec.competencias.context.desc: The right context, at the right size, at the right time.
sec.competencias.system.title: System Design for Agents
sec.competencias.system.desc: Boundaries, contracts, and safe surfaces for change.
sec.competencias.verify.title: Verification Design
sec.competencias.verify.desc: Tests, hooks, reviewers, rollback, and observable evidence.
sec.competencias.note.title: Watch the name
sec.competencias.note.desc: Prompt is an interface. The real skill is architecting the whole system around it: context, memory, tools, validation, feedback, and responsibility.
sec.loop.h2: Same task, higher level of work
sec.loop.intro: The work moves up one level of abstraction. That does not mean it gets easier. It means human error moves location: less syntax, more poor definition of intent, architecture, or evidence.
sec.loop.before.label: Old loop
sec.loop.after.label: Agentic loop
sec.loop.example.title: Example: CSV export in the finance dashboard
sec.loop.row1.new: Define data contract, filters, and permissions
sec.loop.row2.new: Define schema, encoding, timezone, and row limits
sec.loop.row3.new: Map abuse, PII, performance, and audit
sec.loop.row3.evidence: Negative test, auditable log, and timeout
sec.valor.h2: What gains value and what loses relative weight
sec.valor.intro: The change does not make fundamentals irrelevant. It changes which fundamentals separate an average developer from one who can direct agentic systems without creating chaos.
sec.valor.up.label: Becomes more valuable
sec.valor.up.li4: Critical reading of large AI-generated diffs
sec.valor.down.label: Loses relative weight
sec.valor.down.li2: Memorizing framework syntax as the central differentiator
sec.valor.down.li4: Solving isolated problems without product context
sec.valor.down.li5: Knowing the right command without understanding the trade-off
sec.carreira.h2: The traditional career pipeline has been broken
sec.carreira.intro: For years, juniors learned by doing simple, repetitive, safe tasks. If agents do much of that work, basic learning has to be designed on purpose.
sec.carreira.step1.title: The old ramp was repetition
sec.carreira.step1.desc: CRUD, small bug, simple test, local refactor. Learning came from volume and gradual exposure.
sec.carreira.step2.title: Automation removes part of natural practice
sec.carreira.step2.desc: If the agent does the simple task, the junior may lose the path that built code and product intuition.
sec.carreira.step3.title: Formation must become deliberate practice
sec.carreira.step3.desc: Guided PR reading, prompt postmortems, debugging with hypotheses, decomposition exercises, and trade-off reviews.
sec.carreira.rule.title: Rule for technical leaders
sec.carreira.rule.desc: It is not enough to give the team more automation. You have to create spaces where developers learn reasoning, diagnosis, modeling, and validation. Otherwise, the market creates juniors without a ramp and seniors without a base.
sec.anti.h2: Anti-patterns of the developer in an agentic world
sec.anti.intro: Agentic development increases leverage. That also amplifies poor judgment. These behaviors create apparent speed and real debt.
sec.anti.ap1.bad.title: The anxious typist
sec.anti.ap1.bad.desc: Micromanages every line, manually fixes syntax, and turns the agent into expensive autocomplete.
sec.anti.ap1.good.title: The intent architect
sec.anti.ap1.good.desc: Defines contract, constraints, expected evidence, and lets implementation happen inside those limits.
sec.anti.ap2.bad.title: The magic prompt
sec.anti.ap2.bad.desc: Believes a clever sentence replaces context, tests, examples, and acceptance criteria.
sec.anti.ap2.good.title: The context engineer
sec.anti.ap2.good.desc: Builds the right input: docs, memory, constraints, fixtures, tests, and validation plan.
sec.anti.ap3.bad.title: The passive approver
sec.anti.ap3.bad.desc: Accepts a large diff because tests passed and it looks plausible.
sec.anti.ap3.good.title: The systems reviewer
sec.anti.ap3.good.desc: Reviews architecture, observable behavior, product impact, security, and technical debt.
sec.anti.ap4.bad.title: The absent architect
sec.anti.ap4.bad.desc: Lets agents create structure, patterns, and boundaries without human direction.
sec.anti.ap4.good.title: The boundary designer
sec.anti.ap4.good.desc: Defines modules, contracts, and safe areas of change before scaling execution.
sec.evoluir.intro: The transition does not happen through a tool. It happens through a change in practice. Start small, but change the kind of responsibility you take.
sec.evoluir.step1.title: Ask for a plan before code
sec.evoluir.step1.desc: Include risks, files, tests, and rollback criteria before the first edit.
sec.evoluir.step2.title: Write tickets as contracts
sec.evoluir.step2.desc: Behavior, constraints, examples, sensitive data, and success signals.
sec.evoluir.step3.title: Strengthen verification
sec.evoluir.step3.desc: Test behavior, security, performance, observability, and rollback.
sec.evoluir.step4.title: Review by intent
sec.evoluir.step4.desc: Do not review only lines. Review goal, architecture, risk, and evidence.
sec.evoluir.bonus.label: Quick bonus
sec.evoluir.bonus.title: Loop Engineering: the next step after prompting
sec.evoluir.bonus.intro: Instead of prompting the agent at every turn, you design a loop that discovers work, delegates, verifies, records state, and decides the next step.
sec.evoluir.bonus.card1.title: What changes
sec.evoluir.bonus.card1.desc: You stop being the prompt operator and become the designer of the system that triggers agents.
sec.evoluir.bonus.card2.title: Loop pieces
sec.evoluir.bonus.card2.desc: Automation, worktrees, skills, connectors, sub-agents, and external memory that stores state.
sec.evoluir.bonus.card3.title: The risk
sec.evoluir.bonus.card3.desc: A bad loop automates error, cost, and technical debt. Verification remains a human responsibility.
sec.evoluir.bonus.link: Read later: Loop Engineering, by Addy Osmani.
sec.evoluir.mantra.label: Part 12 Mantra
sec.evoluir.mantra.body: The future of the developer is not writing every line. It is deciding what should exist, creating the conditions for agents to build safely, and taking responsibility for the result.
